title: Western volume raised 18-month ENSO forecast error by 6.79% in seasonal ridge models at 2000-2023 origins
abstract: We tested whether western Pacific warm water volume adds 18-month Nino 3.4 forecast skill beyond basin volume, recent history and season. We used fixed NOAA GODAS and ERSSTv5 records. Fits used only targets before the origin year. For 288 monthly origins in 2000-2023, adding western volume raised mean squared error by 6.79%. The conditional 95% three-year block interval for the increase was 1.77% to 13.35%. Root mean squared error rose from 0.862 to 0.891 degrees C. Five-year blocks and two other fixed ridge penalties gave the same sign. Both primary models had higher error than a past-mean forecast. The test does not show that western ocean structure has no physical role or that long-lead ENSO prediction is impossible. Revised data, a short test record and fixed linear models limit inference. Code, source hashes, aggregate scores, score draws, numerical checks and a figure are included. Raw and monthly derived records remain external.

display.caption: Added western volume at 2000-2023 origins. Positive MSE reduction favors western volume. Intervals use paired three-year blocks. Other rows are secondary tests.

citations.reason: Prior shorter-lead western volume and history test motivates this longer-lead conditional comparison. Source data overlap; this is not independent confirmation.
